speaker: paulmcleish
text: Good evening, Councillors. We'll commence the Council meeting now with the opening prayer. Almighty God, we pray for your blessing upon this Council. Help and prosper its work for the advancement and benefit of its people, so that peace and happiness, unity and justice may be established among us all. Amen. Manningham Council acknowledges the Wurundjeri people as the traditional custodians of the land we now know as Manningham. We pay our respects to Wurundjeri elders, past and present, and value the ongoing contribution to the cultural heritage of Manningham. Council would also like to acknowledge the contribution made to Manningham over the years by people of diverse backgrounds and cultures. I welcome all members of the public to this Council meeting this evening. In response to the evolving coronavirus situation, recent changes were made to the Local Government Act, which permit Council meetings to be held virtually for a limited time. The health and safety of our community employees is our priority during these uncertain times. So tonight we are holding our first virtual Council meeting to further reduce the risk of transmission of COVID-19. You will notice a few changes to how we are conducting our meetings, therefore. You won't be able to attend the meeting in person, but you can watch the recording at any time after the meeting when it suits you, as it will be accessible on our website. We are still taking questions from the public and encourage you to submit your questions in accordance with our normal practices prior to the start of the meeting. As you can't be present in the Chamber, your question will be read out and a response will be provided where we have the information to hand. If we're unable to provide a meaningful response, we'll take your question on notice and provide a response in writing. We will deal with a maximum of two questions per person and two questions on any one issue. If you have more than two questions, please submit these through the normal channels in writing to Council. Finally, I would like to advise that if we experience technical issues during the meeting, we will make every attempt to resolve them within 30 minutes. If we're unable to resolve the issue, the meeting will be adjourned until another time and date. A notice will be placed on the Council website advising the meeting has been adjourned and when it is expected to reconvene. So, to the conduct of the meeting. All Council meetings are governed by a meeting procedure local law. I will introduce each item of business as listed on the agenda by calling it by number and reading the title. I will then call for a mover and a seconder of a motion on the item before opening any debate. Only Councillors are obviously able to join the debate. Councillors may adopt the officer's recommendation in the report or propose amendments and supplementary motions. Item two, apologies and request for leave of absence. We have received an apology from Councillor Sophie Galbally for this evening's meeting. What I'll do now is I'd like to confirm the Councillor attendance at the meeting by a show of hand and verbal indication from the individual Councillors. Councillor Mike Zafiropoulos.

speaker: annachen
text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. In quarter three of this financial year, council has completed 117 projects to the value of 21.6 million, which is about 41% of the overall programme, and a further 97 projects started and progressing well. But the overall programme remains behind forecast. It is anticipated that up to 8.1 million in works may not be completed this financial year. The reasons of the delay includes COVID-19 caused uncertainty of delivery and potential restrictions. Some major projects took longer than expected, club requests to delay delivery or change designs, and a number of large projects are likely to be underway by late June. The associate expenditure could fall in before or after 30th of June. The result will be better than expected this financial year, or a very strong start of next financial year. The good news is that considerable progress has been made on the design of projects scheduled for 2020 and 21. This will allow for a quick start to next financial year. As to finance, council has 0.6 million higher than budgeted expenses this quarter because of the January hailstone damages. Therefore, our operating result were below the budget target by 1%, which is 0.4 million. Note that the COVID-19 outbreak is having impact to our finance. The financial impact will be reflected in the 2019 and 20 forecast and the proposed 2020-21 budget. Regarding the corporate performance, council has 13 major initiatives in this financial year. This initiative reflect the back to basic approach of our four-year council plan, including road and park improvements. 11 of the major initiatives are at or above the expected target. For example, council is working on a more inclusive practice for council's front counter, Rofi Lake master plan and Hepburn Park. Design for future road projects are being developed. Our drainage strategy has been revised to focus on a strategic integrated water management response and many, many more. Two initiatives are behind schedule. One is grow the visitor economy initiative because of the tourism industry has been significantly impacted by the social distancing protocol. The other initiative is about local planning. Council is currently conducting community infrastructure needs analysis to better inform the municipal development contribution plan. Therefore, the municipal DCP is deferred and now scheduled for completion in 2021. As for statutory planning, council has made a number of progress improvements over the past few years. Our planning decisions made within the 60 statutory days reached to 97% in March, 2020. One year ago, the rate was only 72%. That is a great improvements. We wish to assure our community that although council's performance in some areas has been impacted because of the COVID-19, officers are proactively looking for innovative and efficient ways to deliver services and activities to continue to meet our community needs in a safe and reasonable way to minimise service disruption and maximise community safety and recovery. Thank you.

text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I've got a couple of questions and they're to do with COVID. And I think Council have done a lot of good work in the community over this COVID lockup that we've had. And a lot of facilities and a lot of Council programs have been put into a different, I suppose, spin, but also some of them have closed down. I'm just asking, first of all, how are we going to inform our community of how things are opening and when they're opening? And more importantly, how are we doing that? I know that we've worked hard with all the different departments during this time when things are closed. I'm sure I've been working very, very hard to work through how they're going to reopen and the steps that they need to take. And I'm sure that as soon as the government announced a time that things can reopen, we would be ready to open pretty well straight away because of the work that we're doing throughout this particular time. I'm just wondering how are we going to let the people know about things like the library opening the date? Because I think that's due to open on the 1st of July. I know that there's another board for that, but our main office, the different tennis courts and things like that. Are we getting any feelers on field sports like football and basketball or what's happening there? Perhaps there is nothing there formally, but what about informal use of those grounds by people and all sorts of other things that we've got running and halls that can be rented out and things like that. Have we got, where could people go to and make a comment about our preparedness to straight away introduce the state government when they relax things, straight away on their timetable, open the things up that should be open.

speaker: paulmcleish
text: Thank you, Councillor. I know that's part of the challenge here is that the government can make an announcement that doesn't actually have the procedures in place for that to be enacted. That's been one of the challenges we had when they made the announcement about sport recently. But I will pass the response to that particular question over to our CEO, Mr. Andrew Day.

speaker: andrewday
text: Thank you, Mayor. And thanks for the question, Councillor Gough. And I agree with your comments in terms of the way that our community in Manningham has handled the shutdown period and also working with us collaboratively on the reopening as well. We've been really pleased with the, particularly the way in which the communities utilised parks and our open spaces in a really responsible way. It's made it really quite simple from a council perspective to be able to continue to provide those services to the community. And we know that a number of councils have had some difficulties with various places and spaces. And we certainly haven't found that challenging in Manningham's areas. So that's been great from our perspective. And you're quite right. We have been working behind the scenes over a period of time since the shutdown to get ready to reopen again. As the mayor said, one of the challenges that we do have is that often we'll get an announcement on the Sunday but potentially not have the guidelines or the regulations either from the state government relevant bodies or the sporting associations in the case of sports immediately on that Monday. So we need to work through what they are and then contact the various groups and we've been doing that. So if I look particularly at a number of areas in relation to sports, for instance, as you rightly point out, Councillor Gough, sports, a number of sports have been able to get active over the last couple of weeks. So we've been working with those sporting groups and sporting associations on what they can and can't do and particularly working with them on their return to play plans. So every sports club needs to have some kind of return to play plan in place to be able to demonstrate things such as cleaning and social distancing and those sorts of things. So we've been actively working with clubs on that front and again, being really pleased with the response from the clubs and a number of those clubs are back up and operating again, albeit in limited form. We're continuing to work with clubs, sports such as football, netball, et cetera, that are a little bit, that have more contact associated with them and indeed have some more restraints around them at the moment and also with their relevant sporting associations to make sure that we're supporting the clubs to develop their plans within the guidelines of those sporting associations as well. So we're working really quickly on that front and I'm really pleased to see a number of clubs up and going already and more to come this week. On Sunday, most people would have seen the announcement from the Premier to be, that enabled us to reopen skate parks and playgrounds and outdoor gyms with a limitation of 10 around them. So we've proceeded to do that. On the Monday, the team did a great job already to go to remove the signs that had been pulled off, put up, I should say, and pulled those signs off and also started to implement the necessary cleaning regime that go along, that goes along with that as well. It's important to note that with all of these reopenings, there are some stringent cleaning requirements that also go along with it. So I won't touch on everything, but I'll come back to where people can find out more information in a moment. Just a couple of key other areas as well. On the 1st of June, we're gonna have some more capability to be able to reopen things like community halls and facilities, again, with restrictions around them in terms of numbers, maintaining that four square metre rule, et cetera. So we've definitely, as Angelo, Mr. Kourambas pointed out in his previous answer to a question in relation to that, we'll have more details on those halls and facilities towards the end of this week and be ready to roll on a number of those. We're gonna particularly focus in on the regular users rather than casual bookings to start with to make sure we get those regular users up and going as quickly as possible. And when they feel comfortable to start to use those facilities a little bit more. Our customer service centre, the plan is to have that up and going on the 1st of June when we're allowed to. And again, we've got all the planning in place for that. And the customer service team, Citizen Connect team have done a great job managing remotely. And it's gonna be great to be able to reopen the Civic Centre here in Doncaster Road to community as well. We're working closely with, just on the pools side of thing, we're working closely with Belgravia who are the providers of that service on behalf of Council at Aqua Arena. There's obviously some fairly strict guidelines around that in terms of number of people that can use lanes, capacity to, well, not to use change rooms at this point in time, mix between indoor and outdoor, not able to use the gym at the moment. Obviously we need to get the heating back up and going in the pools and all of those sort of things. So that's a fairly complex operation, but we've certainly been in constant contact with Belgravia and we'll continue to inform the community when we're ready to roll with the pool. As you pointed out, Councillor Gough, the library has a separate board run on behalf of both Whitehorse and Manningham councils. There's a board meeting on tomorrow night. We'll be able to gather some more information from the library in relation to its preparations to reopen again, and that's certainly listed for the board meeting tomorrow night. So there's some of the key things, but the headline figure in terms of where, or information in terms of where people can find out information is definitely to go to Council's website in the first instance. That's where we placed information for the close down period and that's where we are progressively updating information as facilities come back on deck again. And certainly if there's not enough detail there, we'd recommend that people just give a quick call through to the customer service centre if the detail that they're specifically looking for in terms of their hall or their particular sports facility or place, they've got some queries around it, just feel free to give us a call.
